4807.proof: At x=0 the inequality gives f(0)=0. Choose a in A; then a is nonzero and f(a)>a^2>0. Hence f(a/2) >= f(a)^2/(2a^2) > a^2/2 > (a/2)^2. Thus a/2 is in A. By induction a/2^k belongs to A for every nonnegative integer k. These numbers are pairwise distinct since a is nonzero, proving that A is infinite.

4807.problem: Given that for any real number \( x \), the function \( f(x) \) is defined, and \( f^{2}(x) \leq 2 x^{2} f\left(\frac{x}{2}\right) \). If \( A = \{a \mid f(a) > a^{2}\} \neq \varnothing \), prove that \( A \) is an infinite set.

6651.proof: Set a_(n+1)=a_1. The n ratios a_i/a_(i+1) are positive and their product telescopes to 1. By the arithmetic-geometric mean inequality their sum is at least n times the nth root of 1, hence at least n. Equality holds exactly when all ratios are 1, equivalently all a_i are equal.
